title: Refraction of Light Through a Triangular Glass Prism
subject: physics
learningObjectives: Understand the optical anatomy of an equilateral triangular glass prism including refracting faces, refracting edge, and angle of prism (A).
Trace the path of an incident light ray (PE) undergoing double refraction: entering glass from air (bending towards normal N1N1') and exiting glass into air (bending away from normal N2N2').
Identify and define the Angle of Incidence (i), Angle of Refraction (r), Angle of Emergence (e), and Angle of Deviation (D).
Verify the fundamental geometric relation for a prism: A + D = i + e.
Explain the cause of dispersion of white light into a 7-colour spectrum (ROYGBIV / VIBGYOR) due to wavelength-dependent refractive indices.

scenes.purpose: Introduce the drawing board, white paper sheet fixed with pins, and placement of the triangular glass prism with its boundary outline traced.
Fix optical pins P1 and P2 on the incident beam line, erect normal N1N1', and trace the refracted ray EF travelling through the denser glass medium.
Fix pins P3 and P4 on the emergent ray FS, erect normal N2N2', extend incident and emergent rays to deviation vertex G, and highlight the Angle of Deviation (D).
Demonstrate the dispersion of a composite white light beam into the seven constituent spectrum colours (VIBGYOR) on the observation screen.
